title: Alignment-free discovery of conserved RNA structures in the human genome
summary: RLMHelix combines RNA-language-model dependency maps with thermodynamic pairing probabilities to rank candidate conserved structures. Its genome scan reported 15,821 candidates, two-thirds absent from four earlier screens. The paper compared predicted structures with existing public icSHAPE datasets and sequence-alignment evidence; these retrospective analyses and exploratory pull-downs do not establish prospective or separate-team validation.
ai_technology: RNA language model RLMHelix with thermodynamic structure scoring
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The preprint compared predicted structures against public icSHAPE datasets GSE145805 and GSE74353, including measured RNA cores from five cell lines, and tested conservation/covariation using retrieved alignments. These are existing-data evaluations; pull-down experiments are described as exploratory.
evidence.unknown: The checked source does not report prospective testing before new outcomes or a separate research team's follow-up confirmation; public probing datasets and same-paper exploratory assays support retrospective/benchmark evidence only.
evidence.ai_role: RLMHelix combines RNA-language-model dependency maps with thermodynamic base-pair probabilities, scores helices in single sequences, then tests candidates against alignments; distillation enables genome-scale scans

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
